checks.target: 4.9969 m/s from momentum theory, T = 2 rho A v^2
checks.note: reported, not graded: an actuator disk of finite thickness on a lattice does not have to reproduce the inviscid momentum-theory value, and the graded quantity is a ratio in which the disk's own discretisation cancels. It reads -25.9% on momentum theory

checks.name: heights whose ratio exceeds 1
checks.note: the model approaches 1 from below and cannot exceed it, so a ratio above 1 is the free-air reference being low, not the ground pushing harder. The reference run's floor is an outflow a few radii down rather than infinity, and its induced velocity reads -25.9% on momentum theory -- which is roughly the size of the overshoot. A larger free-air box would tighten it; it is inside the 10% this 1955 model is graded at either way

report: # ground effect: one actuator disk, R 120 mm, T 2.72 N, 12 cells per radius
model:      T_g/T_inf = 1 / (1 - R^2/(16 Z^2)), and the induced-velocity form 1 - (R/4Z)^2 this grades against
reference:  Cheeseman, I.C. and Bennett, W.E. (1955), 'The effect of the ground on a helicopter rotor in forward flight', ARC R&M 3021, equation (2)

caveat:     Three things the usual quotation drops. The ratio is derived AT CONSTANT POWER. Z is the height of the rotor above the ground. The report states no numeric lower bound on Z/R -- only that small Z/R gives 'large errors' and is 'of no practical interest' -- and its one number is in the conclusions, that flight results agree for Z/R greater than 0.6; the Z/R >= 0.25 figure that circulates could not be traced to it. Sanchez-Cuevas, Heredia and Ollero (2017), Int. J. Aerospace Eng. 1823056, measured that a single small rotor follows Cheeseman and Bennett but a complete multirotor does not: the effect is much larger and reaches to about 5R rather than 2R, because of a fountain under the airframe. That is why the graded case here is ONE actuator disk and the quadrotor is a demo rather than a graded comparison
free air:   v 3.7029 m/s measured, 4.9969 m/s from momentum theory
subgrid:    ON (Cs = 0.12); tau_plus 0.50001, so this is an under-resolved large-eddy run
